translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao held the title Prince of Jin he had Pei Xiu draft the revived five noble ranks; only Commandery Duke Fu of Anping kept a ten-thousand-household seat on the old Wei royal scale.

sentences.zh: 其餘縣公邑千八百戶，地方七十五里；

translations.literal: The rest: county dukes' towns one thousand eight hundred households, territory seventy-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Other county dukes drew 1,800 households across seventy-five li square;

sentences.zh: 大國侯邑千六百戶，地方七十里；

translations.literal: Great-state marquises' towns one thousand six hundred households, territory seventy li square;
translations.idiomatic: Marquises of great kingdoms held 1,600 households over seventy li square;

sentences.zh: 次國侯邑千四百戶，地方六十五里；

translations.literal: Next-rank state marquises' towns one thousand four hundred households, territory sixty-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Marquises of secondary kingdoms had 1,400 households and sixty-five li square;

sentences.zh: 大國伯邑千二百戶，地方六十里；

translations.literal: Great-state earls' towns one thousand two hundred households, territory sixty li square;
translations.idiomatic: Great-kingdom earls drew 1,200 households across sixty li;

sentences.zh: 次國伯邑千戶，地方五十五里；

translations.literal: Next-rank state earls' towns one thousand households, territory fifty-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Lesser-kingdom earls had a thousand households over fifty-five li;

sentences.zh: 大國子邑八百戶，地方五十里；

translations.literal: Great-state viscounts' towns eight hundred households, territory fifty li square;
translations.idiomatic: Great-kingdom viscounts received eight hundred households in fifty li square;

sentences.zh: 次國子邑六百戶，地方四十五里；

translations.literal: Next-rank state viscounts' towns six hundred households, territory forty-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Secondary viscounts held six hundred households over forty-five li;

sentences.zh: 男邑四百戶，地方四十里。

translations.literal: Barons' towns four hundred households, territory forty li square.
translations.idiomatic: Baronial seats stopped at four hundred households on forty li square.

sentences.zh: [5]武帝泰始元年，封諸王以郡爲國。

translations.literal: [5] In Jin Emperor Wu's first Taishi year, enfeoffed the various kings taking commanderies as states.
translations.idiomatic: [5] In the first year of Taishi Emperor Wu made each prince's domain a full commandery-sized kingdom.

sentences.zh: 邑二萬戶爲大國，置上中下三軍，兵五千人；

translations.literal: Towns twenty thousand households are a great state; establish upper, middle, and lower three armies—soldiers five thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand households marked a great kingdom with upper, middle, and lower armies totaling five thousand troops;

sentences.zh: 邑萬戶爲次國，置上軍下軍，兵三千人；

translations.literal: Towns ten thousand households are a next-rank state; establish upper army and lower army—soldiers three thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand households made a second-rank kingdom with upper and lower hosts of three thousand soldiers;

sentences.zh: 五千戶爲小國，置一軍，兵千五百人。

translations.literal: Five thousand households are a small state; establish one army—soldiers one thousand five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand households defined a small fief with a single army of fifteen hundred.

translations.literal: Kings did not go to their states; they served in office at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were kept in the capital and never took up residence in their nominal kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 罷五等之制，公侯邑萬戶以上爲大國，五千戶以上爲次國，不滿五千戶爲小國。

translations.literal: Abolished the five-rank system: dukes and marquises' towns ten thousand households and above are great states; five thousand households and above are next-rank states; not filling five thousand households are small states.
translations.idiomatic: When the five-grade scheme was dropped, dukes and marquises above ten thousand households ranked as great fiefs, those above five thousand as middling, and the rest as small.

sentences.zh: 太康元年，平吳，大凡戶二百四十五萬九千八百四十，口一千六百一十六萬三千八百六十三。

translations.literal: Taikang first year, pacified Wu; in all households two million four hundred fifty-nine thousand eight hundred forty, mouths sixteen million one hundred sixty-three thousand eight hundred sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell in the first Taikang year the census added 2,459,840 households and 16,163,863 mouths to the Jin totals.

sentences.zh: 而江左諸國並三分食一，元帝渡江，太興元年，始制九分食一。

translations.literal: Moreover the various states east of the Jiang all together took one-third as food; Yuandi crossed the river; Taixing first year, first regulated one-ninth as food.
translations.idiomatic: Southern principalities had kept a third of their rent for the throne, but after Yuandi crossed the Yangzi the court in Taixing 1 cut the royal share to one-ninth.

translations.literal: Investigate the territory of Yuzhou in the Tribute of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: We now treat the ground classed as Yuzhou in the "Tribute of Yu."

sentences.zh: 及漢武帝，初置司隸校尉，所部三輔、三河諸郡。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, first established the Metropolitan Superintendent; what he administered: the Three Adjuncts, the Three Rivers commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the Metropolitan Superintendent first appeared, overseeing the Three Adjuncts and Three Rivers commands.

sentences.zh: 其界西得雍州之京兆、馮翊、扶風三郡，北得冀州之河東、河內二郡，東得豫州之弘農、河南二郡，郡凡七。

translations.literal: Its boundary: west obtained Yongzhou's Jingzhao, Fengyi, Fufeng three commanderies; north obtained Jizhou's Hedong, Henei two commanderies; east obtained Yuzhou's Hongnong, Henan two commanderies—commanderies in all seven.
translations.idiomatic: Its span took Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng from Yongzhou in the west, Hedong and Henei from Ji in the north, and Hongnong and Henan from Yu in the east—seven commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 位望隆于牧伯，[6]銀印青綬。

translations.literal: Position and outlook loftier than shepherds and regional lords, [6] silver seal, green ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The post outranked provincial governors,[6] bearing a silver seal on green ribbon.

sentences.zh: 及光武都洛陽，司隸所部與前漢不異。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangwu's capital at Luoyang, what the Metropolitan Superintendent administered did not differ from Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu moved the capital to Luoyang the metropolitan belt matched Western Han's layout.

sentences.zh: 魏氏受禪，即都漢宮，司隸所部河南、河東、河內、弘農并冀州之平陽，合五郡，置司州。

translations.literal: The Wei house received abdication, immediately capital at Han palaces; what the Metropolitan Superintendent administered: Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, together with Jizhou's Pingyang—combined five commanderies, established Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took the Han palaces at Luoyang, folded Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, and Pingyang from Ji into one metropolitan zone, and renamed it Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 晉仍居魏都，乃以三輔還屬雍州，分河南立滎陽，分雍州之京兆立上洛，廢東郡立頓丘，遂定名司州，以司隸校尉統之。

translations.literal: Jin still dwelt at Wei's capital; thereupon returned the Three Adjuncts to Yongzhou, split Henan to establish Yingyang, split Yongzhou's Jingzhao to establish Shangluo, abolished Dong commandery to establish Dunqiu, thereupon fixed the name Sizhou, with the Metropolitan Superintendent governing it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin stayed in Wei's Luoyang, sent the Three Adjuncts back to Yongzhou, peeled Yingyang from Henan and Shangluo from Jingzhao, replaced Dong with Dunqiu, and locked in the name Sizhou under the metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 州統郡一十二，縣一百，戶四十七萬五千七百。

translations.literal: The province commands twelve commanderies, one hundred counties, households four hundred seventy-five thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou ruled twelve commanderies and a hundred counties with 475,700 registered households.

translations.literal: Commands twelve counties, households one hundred eleven thousand four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: It governed twelve counties and 111,400 households.

translations.idiomatic: Its wall ran seven li east-west and nine li north-south.

sentences.zh: 東有建春、東陽、清明三門，南有開陽、平昌、宣陽、建陽四門，西有廣陽、西明、閶闔三門，北有大夏、廣莫二門。

translations.idiomatic: East wall opened Jianchun, Dongyang, and Qingming; the south four gates including Kaiyang; the west Guangyang, Ximing, and Changhe; the north Daxia and Guangmo.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉、河南尹及百官列城內也。〉

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Superintendent, Henan governor, and the hundred officials are arrayed within the city.〉
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan commandant, the Henan governor, and the full bureaucracy sat inside those walls.〉

translations.literal: 〈King Xiao of Zhou enfeoffed Duke Hui of Zhou, grandson of Duke Huan of Zhou, at Gong, titled Eastern Zhou; therefore in Warring States times there were Eastern and Western Zhou titles.
translations.idiomatic: 〈King Xiao enfeoffed Duke Hui of Zhou at Gong as "Eastern Zhou," which is why Warring States texts speak of eastern and western Zhou polities.

sentences.zh: 是時遺黎南渡，元帝僑置兗州，寄居京口。

translations.literal: At that time surviving commoners crossed south; Yuandi sojourning established Yanzhou, lodging at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors forded the Yangzi, and Yuan of Jin papered a migrant Yanzhou onto Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 明帝以郗鑒爲刺史，寄居廣陵，置濮陽、濟陰、高平、太山等郡。

translations.literal: Mingdi made Xi Jian inspector, lodging at Guangling, establishing Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming appointed Xi Jian as regional inspector with a seat at Guangling, attaching Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and more nominal commanderies to him.

sentences.zh: 後改爲南兗州，或還江南，或居盱眙，或居山陽。

translations.literal: Later changed to South Yanzhou, sometimes returned south of the river, sometimes dwelt at Xuyi, sometimes dwelt at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The office was rebranded South Yanzhou and drifted between Jiangnan, Xuyi, and Shanyang as the front moved.

sentences.zh: 後始割地爲境，常居廣陵，南與京口對岸。

translations.literal: Later they began to cut land as borders, constantly dwelt at Guangling, south facing Jingkou across the bank.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually real soil was assigned and the seat settled at Guangling, opposite Jingkou on the far shore.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，於北譙界立陳留郡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiankang, on the border of northern Qiao they established Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang four saw a new Chenliu commandery planted along the northern Qiao frontier.

sentences.zh: 安帝分廣陵郡之建陵、臨江、如皋、寧海、蒲濤五縣置山陽郡，屬南兗州。

translations.literal: Emperor An split off Jianling, Linjiang, Rugao, Ninghai, and Putao counties from Guangling commandery to establish Shanyang commandery, belonging to South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An carved five Guangling bayside counties into a Shanyang commandery still listed under South Yanzhou.

translations.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, it is the land between Jing and the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Tribute of Yu maps this belt between the Jing range and the Yellow River.

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: "South of the river is called Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou names the tract south of the river Yuzhou.'

sentences.zh: 」豫者舒也，言稟中和之氣，性理安舒也。

translations.literal: " Yu means ease; saying it receives the harmonious qi, nature and pattern are calm and easeful.
translations.idiomatic: 'Yu' implies ease, because the land drinks in balanced vapors and its temper stays unruffled.'

sentences.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「鉤鈐星別爲豫州。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao says: "The Gou and Qian stars separately become Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanming Bao pairs the Gou-Qian asterisms with Yuzhou.'

sentences.zh: 」地界，西自華山，東至于淮，北自濟，南界荊山。

translations.literal: " Its boundaries: west from Mount Hua, east reaching to the Huai, north from the Ji, south bounded by Mount Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Its compass ran from Mount Hua westward to the Huai eastward, from the Ji northward to Mount Jing southward.'

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，以爲三川、河東、南陽、潁川、碭、泗水、薛七郡。

translations.literal: Qin united all under heaven, making seven commanderies: Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's first map folded the region into Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue commanderies.

sentences.zh: 漢改三川爲河南郡，武帝置十三州，豫州舊名不改，以河南、河東二郡屬司隸，又以南陽屬荊州。

translations.literal: Han changed Sanchuan to Henan commandery; Emperor Wu established thirteen provinces; the old name of Yuzhou was not changed, taking Henan and Hedong two commanderies as belonging to Sili, and further taking Nanyang as belonging to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han retitled Sanchuan Henan, Emperor Wu's thirteen circuits kept the Yuzhou label, while Henan and Hedong answered to Sili and Nanyang slid under Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，改泗水曰沛郡，改碭郡曰梁，改薛曰魯，分梁沛立汝南郡，分潁川立淮陽郡。

translations.literal: Before this, changed Sishui to Pei commandery, changed Dang commandery to Liang, changed Xue to Lu, split Liang and Pei to establish Runan commandery, split Yingchuan to establish Huaiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier rounds had renamed Sishui to Pei, Dang to Liang, Xue to Lu, spun Runan from Liang and Pei, and Huaiyang from Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 後漢章帝改淮陽曰陳郡。

translations.literal: Later Han Emperor Zhang changed Huaiyang to Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han's Emperor Zhang rechristened Huaiyang Chen.

sentences.zh: 魏武分沛立譙郡，魏文分汝南立弋陽郡。

translations.literal: Wei Wu split Pei to establish Qiao commandery; Wei Wen split Runan to establish Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao carved Qiao from Pei, and Cao Pi raised Yiyang from Runan.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受命，又分潁川立襄城郡，分汝南立汝陰郡，合陳郡于梁國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate, again split Yingchuan to establish Xiangcheng commandery, split Runan to establish Ruoyin commandery, and combined Chen commandery into Liang kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sima Yan took the throne he added Xiangcheng from Yingchuan, Ruoyin from Runan, and folded Chen into Liang.

translations.literal: When Liu Yao moved the capital to Chang'an he changed his dynastic title to Zhao; he stationed the joint shepherds of Qin and Liang at Shanggui, the Shuozhou shepherd at Gaoping, the Youzhou inspector at Beidi, and the Bingzhou shepherd at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao crowned himself at Chang'an as Zhao and scattered inspectors—Qin-Liang at Shanggui, Shuozhou at Gaoping, Youzhou on Beidi soil, Bingzhou guarding Puban.

translations.literal: Shi Le captured Chang'an and restored Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le seized Chang'an and resurrected Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 石氏既敗，苻健僭據關中，又都長安，是爲前秦。

translations.literal: After the Shi clan collapsed, Fu Jian seized Guanzhong and again made Chang'an his capital—this is Former Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shi house fell, Fu Jian clamped Guanzhong and enthroned Former Qin at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 於是乃於雍州置司隸校尉，以豫州刺史鎮許昌，秦州刺史鎮上邽，荊州刺史鎮豐陽，洛州刺史鎮宜陽，并州刺史鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: Thereupon they placed a metropolitan colonel at Yongzhou, stationed the Yuzhou inspector at Xuchang, the Qinzhou inspector at Shanggui, the Jingzhou inspector at Fengyang, the Luozhou inspector at Yiyang, and the Bingzhou inspector at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: They carved out a metropolitan colonelcy at Yongzhou while pinning Yuzhou at Xuchang, Qinzhou at Shanggui, Jingzhou at Fengyang, Luozhou at Yiyang, and Bingzhou at Puban.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時，分司隸爲雍州，分京兆爲咸陽郡，洛州刺史鎮陝城。

translations.literal: Under Fu Jian the metropolitan seat became Yongzhou, Jingzhao was split into Xianyang Commandery, and the Luozhou inspector moved to Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian split metropolitan territory into Yongzhou, peeled Xianyang from Jingzhao, and slid Luozhou forward to Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 滅燕之後，分幽州置平州，鎮龍城，幽州刺史鎮薊城，河州刺史鎮枹罕，并州刺史鎮晉陽，豫州刺史鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，雍州刺史鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: After Yan was extinguished they carved Pingzhou from Youzhou with its seat at Longcheng; they stationed the Youzhou inspector at Ji, the Hezhou inspector at Fuhan, the Bingzhou inspector at Jinyang, the Yuzhou inspector at Luoyang, the Yanzhou inspector at Cangyuan, and the Yongzhou inspector at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Once Former Yan fell they raised Pingzhou at Longcheng from Youzhou—inspectors ringed Ji, Fuhan, Jinyang, Luoyang, Cangyuan, and Puban.

sentences.zh: 於是移洛州居豐陽，以許昌置東豫州，以荊州刺史鎮襄陽，徐州刺史鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Then Luozhou was shifted to Fengyang, Dong-Yuzhou was established at Xuchang, the Jingzhou inspector moved to Xiangyang, and the Xuzhou inspector to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou slid south to Fengyang, eastern Yuzhou anchored Xuchang, while Jingzhou and Xuzhou watched Xiangyang and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 既而姚萇滅苻氏，是爲後秦。

translations.literal: Soon Yao Chang extinguished the Fu clan—this is Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang soon erased Former Qin and styled Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 及萇子興克洛陽，以并、冀二州牧鎮蒲阪，豫州牧鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，分司隸領北五郡，置雍州刺史鎮安定。

translations.literal: When Chang's son Xing took Luoyang he stationed joint Bing-Ji shepherds at Puban, the Yu shepherd at Luoyang, the Yanzhou inspector at Cangyuan, split the metropolitan northern five commanderies, and placed a Yongzhou inspector at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing seized Luoyang, stacked Bing-Ji shepherds at Puban, Yu power at Luoyang, Yanzhou at Cangyuan, carved northern metropolitan belts, and parked Yongzhou at Anding.

sentences.zh: 及姚泓爲劉裕所滅，其地尋入赫連勃勃。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong fell to Liu Yu the territory soon passed to Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong perished before Liu Yu and Helian Bobo swallowed the plateau.

sentences.zh: 勃勃僭號於統萬，是爲夏。

translations.literal: Bobo arrogated his title at Tongwan—this is Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo crowned himself at Tongwan as the Xia dynasty.

sentences.zh: 置幽州牧於大城，又平劉義真於長安，遣子璝鎮焉，號曰南臺。

translations.literal: He placed a Youzhou shepherd at Dacheng; after defeating Liu Yizhen at Chang'an he sent his son Gui to hold it, styled the Southern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He named a Youzhou shepherd at Dacheng, crushed Liu Yizhen at Chang'an, left son Gui as viceroy, and dubbed the court Southern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 以朔州牧鎮三城，秦州刺史鎮杏城，雍州刺史鎮陰密，并州刺史鎮蒲阪，梁州牧鎮安定，北秦州刺史鎮武功，豫州牧鎮李閏，[30]荊州刺史鎮陝，其州郡之名並不可知也。

translations.literal: He stationed the Shuozhou shepherd at Sancheng, the Qinzhou inspector at Xingcheng, the Yongzhou inspector at Yinmi, the Bingzhou inspector at Puban, the Liangzhou shepherd at Anding, the Northern Qinzhou inspector at Wugong, the Yu shepherd at Lijian,[30] and the Jingzhou inspector at Shan—the roster of prefectures can no longer be reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors littered Sancheng, Xingcheng, Yinmi, Puban, Anding, Wugong, Lijian,[30] and Shan—later editors lost the exact map.

sentences.zh: 然自元帝渡江，所置州亦皆遙領。

translations.literal: Yet from the time Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangtze every northern province established on the south shore existed only as nominal postings.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan crossed the Great River, northern provinces became empty titles on the left bank.

sentences.zh: 初以魏該爲雍州刺史，鎮酇城，尋省，僑立始平郡，寄居武當城。

translations.literal: First Wei Gai served as Yongzhou inspector at Zancheng; that post was soon abolished and a provisional Shiping Commandery lodged at Wudang fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gai briefly held Yongzhou at Zancheng until the office vanished and Shiping sojourned at Wudang.

sentences.zh: 有秦國流人至江南，改堂邑爲秦郡，僑立尉氏縣屬焉。

translations.literal: When refugees from the Qin princedom reached the southlands Tangyi was renamed Qin Commandery and they planted Weishi County beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin exiles triggered renaming Tangyi to Qin Commandery with Weishi nested inside.

sentences.zh: 康帝時，庾翼爲荊州刺史，遷鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Kang Yu Yi became Jingzhou inspector and shifted his seat to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang ordered Yu Yi west as Jingzhou inspector with seat at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 其後秦雍流人多南出樊沔，孝武始於襄陽僑立雍州，仍立京兆、始平、扶風、河南、廣平、義成、北河南七郡，並屬襄陽。

translations.literal: Later refugees from Qin and Yong poured out through Fan and Mian; Emperor Xiaowu first planted a provisional Yongzhou at Xiangyang together with seven commanderies—Jingzhao, Shiping, Fufeng, Henan, Guangping, Yicheng, and Northern Henan—all subordinate to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin-Yong exiles spilling through Fan and Mian persuaded Emperor Xiaowu to stage Yongzhou at Xiangyang plus seven attached commanderies.

translations.literal: Xiangyang had formerly belonged to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang itself once answered only to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢雍州之西界，周衰，其地爲狄。

translations.literal: By the reckoning of the "Tribute of Yu," this marked Yongzhou's western rim; when Zhou declined the land fell to the Di peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Classical geography marks this as Yongzhou's western bound; Zhou's decay left it to Rong and Di bands.

sentences.zh: 秦興美陽甘泉宮，本匈奴鑄金人祭天之處。

translations.literal: Qin raised its Ganquan palace at Meiyang—the place where the Xiongnu once cast golden men for Heaven sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Ganquan halls at Meiyang echoed the Xiongnu golden idols raised for Heaven.

sentences.zh: 匈奴既失甘泉，又使休屠、渾邪王等居涼州之地。

translations.literal: After the Xiongnu lost Ganquan they stationed the Xiutu and Hunye kings across Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of Ganquan, the Xiongnu parked Xiutu and Hunye across Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二王後以地降漢，漢置張掖、酒泉、敦煌、武威郡。

translations.literal: When both kings later surrendered their lands Han organized Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Wuwei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Their surrender let Han layer Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 其後又置金城郡，謂之河西五郡。

translations.literal: Later Han added Jincheng—the so-called five Hexi commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng joined to complete the five Hexi commands.

sentences.zh: 漢改周之雍州爲涼州，蓋以地處西方，常寒涼也。

translations.literal: Han redesignated Zhou's Yongzhou as Liangzhou because the climate stayed perennially cold.
translations.idiomatic: Han renamed Zhou's Yongzhou Liangzhou for its biting chill.

sentences.zh: 地勢西北邪出，在南山之間，南隔西羌，西通西域，于時號爲斷匈奴右臂。

translations.literal: The terrain angles northwest between southern ranges; it borders the western Qiang on the south and opens toward the Western Regions—contemporaries called it severing the Xiongnu right arm.
translations.idiomatic: The corridor squeezes northwest between ranges, brushes western Qiang, and reaches the Tarim—Han strategists called it amputating the Xiongnu right arm.

sentences.zh: 獻帝時，涼州數有亂，河西五郡去州隔遠，於是乃別以爲雍州。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xian Liangzhou suffered repeated revolts; the five Hexi commanderies lay too far from the provincial seat, so they were separately constituted as Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian's Liangzhou revolts forced the distant Hexi quintet to become their own Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 末又依古典定九州，乃合關右以爲雍州。

translations.literal: Near the dynasty's end the classical nine provinces were invoked and everything west of the passes was folded back into Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han ritualists recombined the western march into one Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏時復分以爲涼州，刺史領戊己校尉，護西域，如漢故事，至晉不改。

translations.literal: Under Wei it was split again into Liangzhou; the inspector retained the Wuji colonel and protected the Western Regions after Han precedent—Jin left that arrangement intact.
translations.idiomatic: Wei split Liangzhou anew, kept the Wuji colonel over the Silk Road, and Jin kept the mold.

sentences.zh: 元康五年，惠帝分敦煌郡之宜禾、伊吾、冥安、深泉、廣至等五縣，分酒泉之沙頭縣，又別立會稽、新鄉，凡八縣爲晉昌郡。

translations.literal: In Yuankang 5 Emperor Hui split Yihu, Yiwu, Ming'an, Shenquan, and Guangzhi—five counties from Dunhuang—and Sha tou county from Jiuquan, added Kuaiji and Xinxiang counties, and formed Jinchang Commandery from eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang 5 carved Jinchang from Dunhuang and Jiuquan scraps plus two new seats.

sentences.zh: 永寧中，張軌爲涼州刺史，鎮武威，上表請合秦雍流移人於姑臧西北，置武興郡，統武興、大城、烏支、襄武、晏然、新鄣、平狄、司監等縣。

translations.literal: During Yongning Zhang Gui served as Liangzhou inspector at Wuwei and memorialized to settle refugees from Qin and Yong northwest of Guzang in Wu Xing Commandery with counties Wuxing, Dacheng, Wuzhi, Xiangwu, Yanran, Xinzhang, Pingdi, and Sijian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui petitioned Yongning courts to plant Qin-Yong exiles northwest of Guzang inside Wu Xing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又分西平界置晉興郡，統晉興、枹罕、永固、臨津、臨鄣、廣昌、大夏、遂興、罕唐、左南等縣。

translations.literal: He also split Xiping's border to create Jinxing Commandery, governing Jinxing, Fuhan, Yonggu, Linjin, Linzhang, Guangchang, Daxia, Suixing, Hantang, Zuonan, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiping he sliced Jinxing Commandery—Jinxing, Fuhan, Yonggu, Linjin, and allies.

sentences.zh: 是時中原淪沒，元帝徙居江左，軌乃控據河西，稱晉正朔，是爲前涼。

translations.literal: While the Central Plains collapsed Emperor Yuan moved south; Zhang Gui held the Hexi corridor and observed Jin calendar—this is Former Liang.
translations.idiomatic: As refugees fled the Yellow River plain, Zhang Gui kept Jin rites alive beyond the passes as Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 及張寔，分金城之令居、枝陽二縣，又立永登縣，合三縣立廣武郡。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhang Shi split Lingju and Zhiyang from Jincheng, further founded Yongdeng County, and from three counties erected Guangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi peeled Lingju and Zhiyang off Jincheng, added Yongdeng, and welded the trio into Guangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 張茂分武興、金城、西平、安故爲定州。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao split Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu to form Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao raised Dingzhou from Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu.

sentences.zh: 張駿分武威、武興、西平、張掖、酒泉、建康、西海、西郡、湟河、晉興、廣武合十一郡爲涼州，[34]興晉、金城、武始、南安、永晉、大夏、武成、漢中爲河州，敦煌、晉昌、高昌、西域都護、戊己校尉、玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun organized Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xi, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwu—eleven commanderies—as Liangzhou,[34] grouped Xingjin, Jincheng, Wushi, Nan'an, Yongjin, Daxia, Wucheng, and Hanzhong as Hezhou, and bundled Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, the Western Regions protector, the Wuji colonel, and Yumen grand protector—three commanderies and three camps—as Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun carved Liangzhou from eleven western seats,[34] stacked another eight into Hezhou, and branded three desert bases Shazhou.

translations.literal: [35]Zhang Jun acted as Liangzhou governor and supervised three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Note [35]: Zhang Jun governed Liangzhou pro tem over three provinces.

sentences.zh: 張祚又以敦煌郡爲商州。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuo further converted Dunhuang Commandery into Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo rechristened Dunhuang as Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永興中，置漢陽縣以守牧地，張玄靚改爲祁連郡。

translations.literal: During Yongxing a Hanyang County was founded to guard pasturelands; Zhang Xuanjing renamed it Qilian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing planted Hanyang for grazing until Zhang Xuanjing styled it Qilian Commandery.

translations.literal: Zhang Tiansi separately established Linsong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiansi added an independent Linsong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 天錫降於苻氏，其地尋爲呂光所據。

translations.literal: When Tiansi surrendered to the Fu clan the territory soon fell to Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Tiansi yielded to Former Qin, Lü Guang seized the corridor.

sentences.zh: 呂光都於姑臧後，以郭黁言讖，改昌松爲東張掖郡。

translations.literal: After Lü Guang moved his capital to Guzang he followed Guo Mo's prophecy-charts and renamed Changsong to East Zhangye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At Guzang Lü Guang listened to Guo Mo's omens and dubbed Changsong Eastern Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 及呂隆降於姚興，其地三分。

translations.literal: When Lü Long surrendered to Yao Xing the land split three ways.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long's capitulation to Yao Xing shattered the plateau into three rivals.

sentences.zh: 武昭王爲西涼，建號於敦煌。

translations.literal: Prince Wuzhao founded Western Liang and raised his standard at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao's Western Liang flew its banner from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤爲南涼，建號於樂都。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu founded Southern Liang and raised his standard at Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu styled Southern Liang from Ledu.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜爲北涼，建號於張掖。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun founded Northern Liang and raised his standard at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun proclaimed Northern Liang at Zhangye.

translations.literal: They divided the five Hexi commanderies among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The trio partitioned the Hexi pentarchy.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢本雍州之域，魏始分隴右置焉，刺史領護羌校尉，中間暫廢。

translations.literal: By the scheme of the "Tribute of Yu" this was Yongzhou soil; Wei first carved Longyou from it; the inspector doubled as Qiang colonel until briefly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Classical Yongzhou fed Wei Longyou commands overseen by a Qiang colonel—sometimes suspended.

sentences.zh: 及泰始五年，又以雍州隴右五郡及涼州之金城、梁州之陰平，合七郡置秦州，鎮冀城。

translations.literal: In Taishi 5 Yongzhou's Longyou quintet plus Jincheng from cool Liangzhou and Yinping from Liang-Han commandery—seven commanderies—were forged into Qinzhou with seat at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 5 welded Yongzhou's Longyou belt, Jincheng from the western Liang corridor, and Yinping from the Hanzhong Liang stack into Qinzhou at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 太康三年，罷秦州，并雍州。

translations.idiomatic: Taikang 3 swallowed Qinzhou back into Yongzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Seven years later Qinzhou returned with seat at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢華陽黑水之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。

sentences.zh: 梁者，言西方金剛之氣強梁，故因名焉。

translations.idiomatic: 'Liang' evokes hard western temper—the label stuck.

translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Rites map paired Liang with Yong.

translations.idiomatic: Han simply treated it as part of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝初平六年，[38]以臨江縣屬永寧郡。

translations.idiomatic: In Chuping 6 Linqing County joined Yongning Commandery, per gloss [38].

sentences.zh: 建安六年，劉璋改永寧爲巴東郡，分巴郡墊江置巴西郡。

translations.literal: Jian'an 6 Liu Zhang renamed Yongning to Badong Commandery and split Dianjiang from Ba Commandery to create Baxia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang converted Yongning into Badong and peeled Baxia from Ba.

sentences.zh: 劉備據蜀，又分廣漢之葭萌、涪城、梓潼、白水四縣，改葭萌曰漢壽，又立漢德縣，以爲梓潼郡；

translations.literal: After Liu Bei seized Shu he split Jiameng, Fucheng, Zitong, and Baishui from Guanghan—renaming Jiameng to Hanshou—and founded Hande County as Zitong Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei carved Zitong Commandery from four Guanghan counties and rechristened Jiameng as Hanshou.

sentences.zh: 割巴郡之宕渠、宣漢、漢昌三縣置宕渠郡，尋省，以縣並屬巴西郡。

translations.literal: He cut Dangqu, Xuanhan, and Hanchang from Ba Commandery to plant Dangqu Commandery; soon it was abolished and the counties reverted to Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dangqu Commandery lasted briefly before its seats slid back into Ba.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，分益州，立梁州於漢中，改漢壽爲晉壽，又分廣漢置新都郡。

translations.literal: Taishi 3 split Yizhou, planted Liangzhou at Hanzhong, renamed Hanshou to Jinshou, and split Guanghan to create Xindu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 3 raised Liangzhou at Hanzhong, upgraded Hanshou to Jinshou, and spun Xindu from Guanghan.

translations.idiomatic: Taikang 6, ninth month, folded Xindu back into Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 惠帝復分巴西置宕渠郡，統宕渠、漢昌、宣漢三縣，并以新城、魏興、上庸合四郡以屬梁州。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui again split Baxi to recreate Dangqu Commandery—governing Dangqu, Hanchang, and Xuanhan—and grouped it with Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong into four commands under Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui revived Dangqu from Baxi and bundled four frontier commands under Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋而梁州郡縣沒于李特，永嘉中又分屬楊茂搜，其晉人流寓於梁益者，仍於二州立南北二陰平郡。

translations.literal: Soon Liangzhou folds fell to Li Te; during Yongjia they passed piecemeal to Yang Maosou; Jin refugees drifted into Liang-Yi and spawned northern and southern Yinping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te swallowed Liangzhou seats; Yongjia fragments entered Yang Maosou's sphere; exiles duplicated Yinping north and south.

sentences.zh: 及桓溫平蜀之後，以巴漢流人立晉昌郡，領長樂、安晉、延壽、安樂、宣漢、寧都、新興、吉陽、東關、永安十縣；

translations.literal: After Huan Wen pacified Shu he planted Jinchang Commandery for Ba-Han refugees—supervising Chang'an, Anjin, Yanshou, Anle, Xuanhan, Ningdu, Xinxing, Jiyang, Dongguan, and Yong'an—ten counties;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's Shu campaign yielded Jinchang Commandery with ten refugee counties.

sentences.zh: 又置益昌、晉興二縣，屬巴西郡；

translations.literal: He added Yichang and Jinxing counties under Ba Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Yichang and Jinxing nestled inside Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 於德陽界東南置遂寧郡；

translations.literal: He established Suining Commandery southeast of Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: Suining appeared southeast of Deyang.

sentences.zh: 又於晉壽置劍閣縣，屬梁州。

translations.literal: Jiange County was also founded at Jinshou and placed under Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court planted Jiange County under Jinshou's Liangzhou umbrella.

sentences.zh: 後孝武分梓潼北界立晉壽郡，統晉壽、白水、邵歡、興安四縣；

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowu split Zitong's northern frontier to erect Jinshou Commandery, governing Jinshou, Baishui, Shaohuan, and Xing'an counties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu peeled Jinshou Commandery from northern Zitong with four counties.

sentences.zh: 梓潼郡徙居梓潼，罷劍閣縣；

translations.literal: Zitong Commandery relocated its seat to Zitong and abolished Jiange County.
translations.idiomatic: The Zitong headquarters slid homeward and Jiange vanished.

sentences.zh: 又別置南漢中郡，分巴西、梓潼爲金山郡。

translations.literal: Southern Hanzhong Commandery was separately established and Ba together with Zitong yielded Jinshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Hanzhong appeared while Ba and Zitong fed Jinshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及安帝時，又立新巴、汶陽二郡，又有北新巴、華陽、南陰平、北陰平四郡，其後又立巴渠、懷安、宋熙、白水、上洛、北上洛、南宕渠、懷漢、新興、安康等十郡。

translations.literal: Under Emperor An there came Xinba and Wenyang commanderies, plus Northern Xinba, Huayang, southern and northern Yinping—four more—and later Baqu, Huai'an, Songxi, Baishui, Shangluo, northern Shangluo, southern Dangqu, Huaihan, Xinxing, and Ankang—ten commanderies all told.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An's reign stacked refugee commands until ten more prefectures cluttered the map.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢及舜十二牧俱爲梁州之域，周合梁於雍，則又爲雍州之地。

translations.literal: By the "Tribute of Yu" and Shun's twelve pastures this soil belonged to Liangzhou; Zhou folded Liang into Yong, so it counts as Yongzhou ground.
translations.idiomatic: Classical Liangzhou melted into Yong once Zhou paired Liang with Yong.

sentences.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「參伐流爲益州，益之爲言阨也。

translations.literal: The *Spring and Autumn Yuan Ming Bao* states: "The asterism Shen-Wei flows aside to become Yizhou; yi speaks of constriction."
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal *Yuan Ming Bao* ties Yizhou's name to Shen-Wei stars and narrow passes.

sentences.zh: 」言其所在之地險阨也，亦曰疆壤益大，故以名焉。

translations.literal: "It refers to how precipitous the ground is; another gloss says its borders swell outward—hence the epithet."
translations.idiomatic: Commentators gloss yi as perilous terrain—or ever-widening frontier.

sentences.zh: 始秦惠王滅蜀，置郡，以張若爲蜀守。

translations.literal: King Hui of Qin was first to extinguish Shu, install a commandery, and appoint Zhang Ruo as governor of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin's King Hui swallowed Shu he parked Zhang Ruo as prefect.

sentences.zh: 及始皇置三十六郡，蜀郡之名不改。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor founded thirty-six commanderies the name Shu Commandery stayed unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Even Qin Shihuang's thirty-sixfold reform kept Shu Commandery.

translations.literal: Early Han listed Hanzhong, Ba, and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han knew three Ba-Shu units.

sentences.zh: 高祖六年，分蜀置廣漢，凡爲四郡。

translations.literal: Gaozu's sixth year split Shu to create Guanghan—four commands altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu carved Guanghan from Shu for a quartet of western prefectures.

sentences.zh: 武帝開西南夷，更置犍爲、牂柯、越巂、益州四郡，凡八郡，遂置益州統焉，益州蓋始此也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu opened the southwestern Yi and added Qianwei, Zangke, Yuexi, and Yizhou commanderies—eight in all—then instituted Yizhou province over them; Yizhou begins here.
translations.idiomatic: Han Emperor Wu's Yi thrust forged eight commands before stacking them under Yizhou province.

sentences.zh: 及後漢，明帝以新附置永昌郡，安帝又以諸道置蜀、廣漢、犍爲三郡屬國都尉，及靈帝又以汶江、蠶陵、廣柔三縣立汶山郡。

translations.literal: Later Han's Ming Emperor added Yongchang for new tribes; An Emperor added Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei dependent states; Ling Emperor raised Wenshan Commandery from Wenjiang, Canling, and Guangrou counties.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han layered Yongchang, dependent prefectures, and Wenshan onto the southwest.

sentences.zh: 獻帝初平元年，劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Xian's first year of Chuping Liu Zhang split Ba Commandery to plant Yongning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping 1 saw Liu Zhang peel Yongning from Ba.

sentences.zh: [42]建安六年，改永寧爲巴東，以巴郡爲巴西，又立涪陵郡。

translations.literal: Collation gloss forty-two: Jian'an 6 renamed Yongning to Badong, designated Ba as Baxi, and founded Fuling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The forty-second apparatus note records Jian'an 6 renaming Yongning into Badong, folding Ba into Baxi, and planting Fuling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，劉備分巴郡立固陵郡。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year Liu Bei split Ba Commandery to erect Guling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-one Liu Bei drew Guling Commandery out of Ba.

sentences.zh: 蜀章武元年又改固陵爲巴東郡，巴西郡爲巴郡，又分廣漢立梓潼郡，分犍爲立江陽郡，以蜀郡屬國爲漢嘉郡，以犍爲屬國爲朱提郡。

translations.literal: Shu Han Zhangwu 1 renamed Guling to Badong, Baxi back to Ba Commandery, split Guanghan for Zitong, split Qianwei for Jiangyang, converted Shu dependent state into Hanjia Commandery, and Qianwei dependent state into Zhuti Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's Zhangwu edicts rewired Ba-Shu names across the basin.

sentences.zh: 劉禪建興二年，改益州郡爲建寧郡，廣漢屬國爲陰平郡，分建寧永昌立雲南郡，分建寧牂柯立興古郡，分廣漢立東廣漢郡。

translations.literal: Liu Shan Jianxing 2 converted Yizhou Commandery to Jianning, Guanghan dependent state to Yinping Commandery, split Jianning and Yongchang for Yunnan Commandery, split Jianning and Zangke for Xinggu Commandery, and split Guanghan for Eastern Guanghan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan's Jianxing reforms multiplied southern commands.

sentences.zh: 魏景元中，蜀平，省東廣漢郡。

translations.literal: Wei Jingyuan era Shu fell and Eastern Guanghan Commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wei annexation canceled Eastern Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 及武帝泰始二年，分益州置梁州，以漢中屬焉。

translations.idiomatic: Taishi 2 lifted Liangzhou from Yizhou and parked Hanzhong inside.

translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong peeled Shenli and Hanyuan from Hanjia and Shu.

sentences.zh: 是時益州郡縣雖沒李氏，江左並遙置之。

translations.literal: Though Li clan maps swallowed Yizhou, exiles south of the Yangtze kept phantom postings.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers beyond the river maintained empty registers.

sentences.zh: 桓溫滅蜀，其地復爲晉有，省漢原、沈黎而立南陰平、晉原、寧蜀、始寧四郡焉。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen extinguished Shu Jin recovered the soil, abolished Hanyuan and Shenli, and founded southern Yinping, Jinnning, Ningshu, and Shining commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's victory restored Jin lines—four fresh commands replaced Li Xiong's pairs.

sentences.zh: 咸安二年，益州復沒於苻氏。

translations.literal: Xian'an 2 lost Yizhou again to the Fu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian'an 2 handed Yizhou back to Former Qin.

translations.literal: Taiyuan 8 Jin recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan 8 returned the basin to Jin.

sentences.zh: 隆安二年，又立晉熙、遂寧、晉寧三郡云。

translations.literal: Long'an 2 founded Jinxi, Suining, and Jinning commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Long'an 2 raised Jinxi, Suining, and Jinning.

translations.literal: Under Han and Wei this counted as Yizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Han-Wei archives label it Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，武帝以益州地廣，分益州之建寧、興古、雲南、交州之永昌，合四郡爲寧州，統縣四十五，戶八萬三千。

translations.literal: Taishi 7 Emperor Wu split vast Yizhou: Jianning, Xinggu, Yunnan from Yizhou plus Yongchang from Jiao Province—four commands—became Ningzhou with forty-five counties and eighty-three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 7 carved Ningzhou from four southwestern commands.

translations.literal: Yunnan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunnan commandery.

translations.literal: 〈Shu Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shu regime.

translations.literal: It governs nine counties; households nine thousand two hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: Nine counties and nine thousand two hundred households.〉

sentences.zh: 雲平 雲南 梇棟 青蛉 姑復 邪龍 楪榆 遂久 永寧

translations.literal: Yunping Yunnan Longdong Qingling Gufu Xielong Dieyu Suijiu Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Yunping, Yunnan, Longdong, Qingling, Gufu, Xielong, Dieyu, Suijiu, and Yongning counties.

translations.literal: Xinggu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinggu commandery.

translations.literal: 〈Shu Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shu regime.

translations.literal: It governs eleven counties; households six thousand two hundred.〉
translations.idiomatic: Eleven counties and six thousand two hundred households.〉

sentences.zh: 律高 句町 宛溫 漏臥 毋掇[45]賁古 滕休 鐔封[46]漢興 進乘 都篖

translations.literal: Lügao Gouting Wanwen Louwo Wuduo[45] Bengui Tengxiu Tanfeng[46] Hanxing Jincheng Doulang.
translations.idiomatic: Lügao, Gouting, Wanwen, Louwo, Wuduo,[45] Bengui, Tengxiu, Tanfeng,[46] Hanxing, Jincheng, and Doulang counties.

translations.literal: Jianning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianning commandery.

translations.literal: 〈Shu Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shu regime.

translations.literal: It governs seventeen counties; households twenty-nine thousand.〉
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen counties and twenty-nine thousand households.〉

sentences.zh: 味 昆澤 存䣖 新定 談槀 母單 同瀨 漏江 牧麻 穀昌 連然 秦臧 雙柏 俞元 修雲 泠丘 滇池

translations.literal: Wei Kunze Cunpi Xinding Tangao Mudan Tonglai Loujiang Muma Guchang Lianran Qinzang Shuangbai Yuyuan Xiuyun Lingqiu Dianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Kunze, Cunpi, Xinding, Tangao, Mudan, Tonglai, Loujiang, Muma, Guchang, Lianran, Qinzang, Shuangbai, Yuyuan, Xiuyun, Lingqiu, and Dianchi counties.

translations.literal: Yongchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchang commandery.

translations.literal: 〈Han established it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Han foundation.

translations.literal: It governs eight counties; households thirty-eight thousand.〉
translations.idiomatic: Eight counties and thirty-eight thousand households.〉

sentences.zh: 不韋 永壽 比蘇 雍鄉 南涪 巂唐 哀牢 博南

translations.literal: Buwei Yongshou Bisu Yongxiang Nanfu Zuitang Ailao Bonan.
translations.idiomatic: Buwei, Yongshou, Bisu, Yongxiang, Nanfu, Zuitang, Ailao, and Bonan counties.

sentences.zh: 太康三年，武帝又廢寧州入益州，立南夷校尉以護之。

translations.literal: Taikang 3 Emperor Wu abolished Ningzhou into Yizhou and planted a southern Yi colonel to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 3 folded Ningzhou back into Yizhou under a southern Yi colonel.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，惠帝復置寧州，又分建寧以西七縣別立爲益州郡。

translations.literal: Tai'an 2 Emperor Hui restored Ningzhou and split seven counties west of Jianning into a separate Yizhou Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tai'an 2 revived Ningzhou and spawned another Yizhou Commandery west of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年，改益州郡曰晉寧，分牂柯立平夷、夜郎二郡。

translations.literal: Yongjia 2 renamed Yizhou Commandery to Jinning and split Zangke into Pingyi and Yelang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia 2 rechristened Yizhou Commandery as Jinning and bisected Zangke.

translations.literal: Collation gloss forty-seven: yet by then Li Te again owned the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Gloss forty-seven reminds readers that Li Te once again seized those counties before Jin returned.

sentences.zh: 其後李壽分寧州興古、永昌、雲南、朱提、越巂、河陽六郡爲漢州。

translations.literal: Later Li Shou split six Ningzhou commands—Xinggu, Yongchang, Yunnan, Zhuti, Yuexi, Heyang—into Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou carved Hanzhou from six southern commands.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，分牂柯、夜郎、朱提、越巂四郡置安州。

translations.literal: Xiankang 4 organized Anzhou from Zangke, Yelang, Zhuti, and Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang 4 stacked Anzhou atop four frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 八年，又罷并寧州，以越巂還屬益州，省永昌郡焉。

translations.literal: Year eight abolished it back into Ningzhou, returned Yuexi to Yizhou, and abolished Yongchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later Jin dissolved Anzhou, reassigned Yuexi, and struck Yongchang.

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 崆山訪道「崆」，宋本、局本等作「風」，殿本作「崆」，今從殿本。

translations.literal: Regarding "Kong mountain seeking the Way": Song woodblocks and Bureau editions read "wind"; the Palace edition reads "Kong"; this edition follows the Palace text.
translations.idiomatic: Editors prefer Palace "Kong" over Song "wind" for the sacred peak.

sentences.zh: 黃帝于崆峒山訪道，傳自莊子。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor sought the Way at Kongtong Mountain according to Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi places the Yellow Emperor's Kongtong pilgrimage.

sentences.zh: 義陽據下「武帝增置」之文及「義陽郡」下之文，義陽郡又置于晉武帝太康時。

translations.literal: Yiyang: comparing later passages on "Emperor Wu added seats" and the Yiyang Commandery entry shows Yiyang was founded under Jin Emperor Wu's Taikang era.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-headings prove Yiyang belongs to Emperor Wu's Taikang expansions.

sentences.zh: 永壽三年戶千六十七萬七千九百六十口五千六百四十八萬六千八百五十六後漢書郡國志在本志校記中以後簡稱《續漢志·一》注云：「永壽二年，戶千六百七萬九百六，口五千六萬六千八百五十六人。」

translations.literal: Yongshou three-year household count diverges from Fan Ye's annotation citing Yongshou two—figures reproduced here as transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongshou census clashes with Fan Ye's Yongshou two gloss.

sentences.zh: 嗣王之庶子爲亭侯各本無「亭」字，殿本有。

translations.literal: The collateral heir-king's son becomes ting marquis: various editions omit ting; Palace prints include it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace editions insert ting before marquis.

sentences.zh: 今從殿本，與魏志文帝紀合。

translations.literal: We follow the Palace edition, matching Wei Emperor Wen's annals.
translations.idiomatic: Palace wording aligns with Wei Emperor Wen's record.

sentences.zh: 位望隆于牧伯「隆」，各本作「降」，宋本作「隆」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Rank prestige rises above shepherds: editions write "fall" except Song prints reading "rise"; we adopt Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song's "rise" fits context better than "fall".

sentences.zh: 縣一百戶四十七萬五千七百下所列爲縣九十九，戶四十九萬二千四百。

translations.literal: Text lists ninety-nine counties yet tallies forty-nine thousand two hundred forty households below.
translations.idiomatic: The county tally reads ninety-nine while households hit forty-nine thousand two hundred forty.

sentences.zh: 兩數不合，各州頗有此類情況，以後不具校。

translations.literal: The mismatch repeats across provinces; later collations note rather than reconcile each instance.
translations.idiomatic: Editors flag such mismatches once rather than line by line.

sentences.zh: 有博浪長沙張良擊秦始皇處 畢沅《晉書·地理志·新補正》

translations.literal: "Site where Zhang Liang struck the First Emperor at Bolangsha" — Bi Yuan's *New Rectifications to the Jin Shu Geography Treatise*
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan's collation cites Zhang Liang's Bolangsha blow against Qin Shihuang.

translations.literal: (Hereafter cited as *Bi's Collations*)
translations.idiomatic: (Hereafter *Bi's Collations*)

sentences.zh: 謂「遍檢諸地志，皆云博浪沙在陽武。

translations.literal: states that "having surveyed every geographical treatise, all place Bolang Sands in Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan opens by insisting every gazetteer parks Bolang Sands at Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 」疑此十二字注本在「陽武」下，錯簡入卷縣耳。

translations.literal: "」These twelve gloss characters should sit beneath ‘Yangwu’ in the note; they were slipped by misplaced bamboo slips into the Juan county entry."
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan argues a dozen commentary graphs belong under Yangwu, not with Juan county.

sentences.zh: 分京兆南部置「部」，各本作「郡」，宋本作「部」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Splitting the southern part of Jingzhao to establish a ‘bu’: editions read ‘jun’ except Song prints reading ‘bu’; we follow Song.
translations.idiomatic: Editors adopt Song's ‘bu’ where others misread ‘jun’.

sentences.zh: 汾陽公國相 《畢校》及方愷《新校·晉書·地理志》

translations.literal: Chancellor of Fenyang ducal state — Bi Yuan's collations and Fang Kai's *New Collations to Jin Shu Geography*
translations.idiomatic: Heading cites Bi Yuan and Fang Kai's apparatus.

translations.literal: (Hereafter *Fang's Collations*)
translations.idiomatic: (Hereafter *Fang's Collations*)

translations.literal: Both insist ‘Fenyang’ ought to read ‘Fenyin.’
translations.idiomatic: Bi and Fang emend Fenyang to Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 按：「公國相」，各本作「公相國」，「相國」二字誤倒，宋本不誤，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Commentary: editions invert ‘ducal chancellor’ as ‘chancellor duke’; Song preserves the proper order—follow Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song correctly orders ‘ducal chancellor’ versus transposed prints.

sentences.zh: 清泉考異：本「清淵」，避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Qingquan textual note: the original read Qingyuan, altered to skirt Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Tang scribes dodged taboo by renaming Qingyuan Qingquan.

sentences.zh: 大戚考異：大戚即廣戚，隋避煬帝諱改。

translations.literal: Daqi textual note: Daqi is Guangqi, renamed under Sui to avoid Emperor Yang's taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Sui editors swapped Guangqi for Daqi.

sentences.zh: 兗端也「端」，各本作「瑞」，今從宋本作「端」。

translations.literal: ‘Yan ends here’ — editions write ‘auspicious’ except Song's ‘end’; adopt Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song's ‘terminus’ beats other prints’ ‘omen.’

sentences.zh: 魏武帝封考異：袁廷檮曰，「武帝」當作「元帝」，即常道鄉公也。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wu enfeoffment gloss: Yuan Tingtao argues ‘Emperor Wu’ should read ‘Emperor Yuan,’ i.e., the Duke of Changdao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tingtao corrects the ruler named on the marquisate.

translations.literal: When Jin received the abdication he was invested as Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin transfer invested him prince at Chenliu.

translations.literal: Jiyin Commandery originally wrote ‘Jiyang Commandery.’
translations.idiomatic: Headline mistakenly said Jiyang for Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 考異：漢無濟陽郡，蓋「濟陰」之誤。

translations.literal: Textual note: Han never had Jiyang Commandery—it must be a slip for Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Han sources prove Jiyang impossible here.

sentences.zh: 卞壺傳濟陰冤句人，宋書州郡志於城武、離狐二縣並云晉太康地志屬濟陰。

translations.literal: Bi Kan's biography calls him a Yuanyuan man from Jiyin; Liu Song's treatise labels Chengwu and Lihu under Jiyin in Jin Taikang registers.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel passages anchor Jiyin, not Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 按：《左傳》隱公七年杜注及郤詵傳並可證。

translations.literal: Commentary: Zuo Duke Yin 7 Du Yu gloss plus Xi Shen's biography corroborate.
translations.idiomatic: Commentarial tradition backs the emendation.

translations.literal: Accordingly we emend.
translations.idiomatic: Editors adopt the correction.

sentences.zh: 宛句卞壺傳作「冤句」，《漢書·地理志》在本志校記中以後簡稱漢志上、《續漢志·三》、宋書州郡志在本志校記中以後簡稱宋志一、魏書地形志在本志校記中以後簡稱後魏志二、隋書地理志在本志校記中以後簡稱隋志中並作「冤句」。

translations.literal: Wanju — Bi Kan's text writes Yuanju; Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise III, Liu Song treatise (abbreviated Song Treatise I), Wei Treatise II, Sui Treatise II spell Yuanju uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Kan's biography writes Yuanju while Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise III, Liu Song's prefectural roster, Wei geography, and Sui geography all agree on Yuanju for this seat.

translations.literal: Hulu originally appeared as ‘Luhu.’
translations.idiomatic: Characters were reversed to Luhu.

sentences.zh: 舉正：當作「湖陸」，見《左傳》襄公十九年杜注。

translations.literal: Correction: should read Hulu—see Zuo Duke Xiang 19 Du Yu gloss.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu confirms Hulu order.

sentences.zh: 斠注：水經濟水、泗水注亦作「湖陸」。

translations.literal: Jiao commentary: Shui Jing's Ji and Si chapters likewise write Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Hydrological glosses agree.

sentences.zh: 按：漢志上、《續漢志·三》謂本曰湖陵，莽改湖陸。

translations.literal: Commentary: Han Treatise I and Xu Han Treatise III say it was originally Huling, Wang Mang renamed Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Historical nomenclature traces Wang Mang's tweak.

translations.literal: Text adjusted accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Characters now match canonical order.

sentences.zh: 烏下聚馬與龍晉書地理志注後簡稱馬校：「烏」當作「嶲」。

translations.literal: ‘Wuxia settlement’ — Ma Xu's Jin geography commentary: ‘Wu’ should read ‘Xi.’
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xu emends bird radical.

sentences.zh: 《續漢志·三》作「嶲下聚」，劉昭注引《左傳》僖公二十六年杜注作「嶲下」。

translations.literal: Xu Han Treatise III reads ‘Xixia settlement’; Liu Zhao cites Zuo Duke Xi 26 Du Yu as ‘Xixia.’
translations.idiomatic: Parallel passages demand Xi.

translations.literal: Nancheng originally read ‘Nanwucheng.’
translations.idiomatic: Extra ‘Wu’ infected Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 考異：景獻羊皇后、惠羊皇后、羊祜傳、宋書羊欣、羊元保傳並云泰山南城人，宋、齊、隋志皆稱南城，惟晉志多一「武」字，殆因下文有「南武陽」而衍一「武」字。

translations.literal: Textual note: Empresses Jingxian and Hui, Yang Hu's biography, Liu Song Yang Xin and Yang Yuanbao biographies all say Taishan Nancheng—Song, Qi, and Sui treatises agree—only Jin Treatise adds ‘Wu,’ probably bleeding from ‘Nanwuyang’ below.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jingxian, Empress Hui, Yang Hu, Yang Xin, and Yang Yuanbao uniformly call them Taishan Nancheng natives; Song, Qi, and Sui gazetteers likewise omit the stray wu graph that Jin duplicated from Nanwuyang.

translations.literal: Commentary: Qian's judgment stands; delete accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Editors strip the intrusive graph.

translations.literal: Mou originally read ‘Eastern Mou.’
translations.idiomatic: Erroneous ‘east’ prefix.

translations.literal: Textual note: the character ‘east’ is redundant.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators reject the extra graph.

sentences.zh: 漢志上、《續漢志·三》泰山郡有牟縣，即春秋牟國，與東萊之東牟非一地。

translations.literal: Han Treatise I and Xu Han Treatise III list Mou County under Taishan—the ancient Mou state—not Eastern Lai's Eastern Mou.
translations.idiomatic: Geography distinguishes homophonous seats.

sentences.zh: 羊祜傳詔以泰山之南武陽、牟、南城、梁父、平陽爲南城郡，是晉時已名牟縣也。

translations.literal: Yang Hu's edict naming Nanwuyang, Mou, Nancheng, Liangfu, and Pingyang as Nancheng Commandery proves Jin already called it Mou County.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial mandate confirms Mou without ‘east.’

sentences.zh: 按：宋志一、《左傳》桓公十五年注「泰山牟縣」，均亦無「東」字，今據刪。

translations.literal: Commentary: Song Treatise I and Zuo Duke Huan 15 gloss ‘Taishan Mou County’ likewise lack ‘east’—delete.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel citations justify deletion.

sentences.zh: 長平馬校：縣已見前潁川郡，此誤複出。

translations.literal: Changping — Ma Xu: the county already appeared under Yingchuan; repetition here is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicate Changping entry flagged.

sentences.zh: 竺邑 《方校》：武陔傳，「沛國竹邑人」，此作「竺邑」，似誤。

translations.literal: Zhu yi — Fang's collations: Wu Ling's biography reads ‘Zhuyi’ in Pei—‘Zhu yi’ here seems wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Kai questions bamboo versus Zhu.

sentences.zh: 斠注：魏志明紀、胡質傳引虞預晉書、宋書州郡志、水經睢水注引李奇說皆作「竹邑」。

translations.literal: Jiao commentary: Wei Emperor Ming's annals, Hu Zhi's biography citing Yu Yu's Jin Shu, Liu Song treatise, and Shui Jing's Sui chapter citing Li Qi all write Zhuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Broad manuscript tradition favors Zhuyi.

sentences.zh: 竺邑即竹邑，本漢縣，有竹邑侯張壽碑。

translations.literal: Zhuyi matches ancient Zhuyi, a Han county documented on Marquis Zhang Shou's Zhuyi stele.
translations.idiomatic: Epigraphy confirms Zhuyi.

sentences.zh: 按：《漢志·上》、《續漢志·二》、《後漢書·明八王傳》、《吳志·薛綜傳》、《隋志·下》彭城郡符離下注並作「竹」。

translations.literal: Commentary: Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise II, Later Han Ming princes, Wu Zhi's biography, and Sui Treatise under Peicheng Fuli all write ‘bamboo.’
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo radical prevails in canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 蕃各本作「番」，今從宋本作「蕃」，與漢志下、《續漢志·二》合。

translations.literal: Fan: editions write ‘Fan’ except Song's ‘Fan’—follow Song to match Han Treatise II and Xu Han Treatise II.
translations.idiomatic: Song preserves Fan graph.

sentences.zh: 縣八十三「三」，各本作「二」，今從殿本作「三」，與實領縣數合。

translations.literal: ‘Eighty-three counties’ — editions read ‘two’ for the third digit; Palace prints ‘three,’ matching actual totals.
translations.idiomatic: Palace arithmetic aligns with county counts.

sentences.zh: 易城漢志上、《續漢志·二》、後魏志上及後漢書劉虞傳並無「城」字。

translations.literal: Yicheng — Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise II, Wei Treatise I, and Fan Ye's Liu Yu biography lack ‘city.’
translations.idiomatic: Earlier gazetteers omit the suffix.

sentences.zh: 戶一萬八千一百「八千」，各本作「六千」，今從殿本作「八千」，與統計戶數相符。

translations.literal: Households eighteen thousand one hundred — editions read ‘six thousand’ for the middle figure; Palace prints ‘eight thousand,’ matching statistical rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Palace household figures reconcile.

sentences.zh: 陰氣雍閼也「陰」下原有「陽」字。

translations.literal: ‘Yin vapors blocked’ originally carried an extra ‘yang’ after ‘yin.’
translations.idiomatic: Erroneous yang character intruded.

sentences.zh: 斠注：類聚六、御覽一六四引太康地記均無「陽」字。

translations.literal: Jiao commentary: Taiping Imperial Digest 6 and Imperial Readings 164 cite Taikang Records without ‘yang.’
translations.idiomatic: Early encyclopedias omit yang.

translations.literal: Commentary: deleting ‘yang’ is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Editors remove yang.

sentences.zh: 始平郡泰始二年置「二」，各本作「三」，今從宋本作「二」，與宋志三合。

translations.literal: Shiping Commandery founded Taishi second year — editions read ‘three’ except Song's ‘two,’ agreeing with Song Treatise III.
translations.idiomatic: Song Taishi date prevails.

sentences.zh: 徙都 疑此二字因涉下文「徙都長安」而誤衍。

translations.literal: ‘Moved the capital’ — suspect these characters wrongly duplicated from ‘moved capital to Chang'an’ below.
translations.idiomatic: Likely scribal duplication.

sentences.zh: 李閏姚萇載記、魏書安定王燮傳皆作「李潤」。

translations.literal: Li Run — Yao Chang's biography and Wei Emperor Ding's biography both write Li Run.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel texts read Li Run.

sentences.zh: 避文帝諱改也「文」，原誤作「景」，今改正。

translations.literal: ‘Avoided Emperor Wen's taboo’ — ‘Wen’ was mistakenly written ‘Jing’; corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Taboo note restored to Wen.

translations.literal: Ming'an — original wrote ‘Yi'an.’
translations.idiomatic: Yi misprinted for Ming.

sentences.zh: 《畢校》：應作「冥安」，《元和郡縣志》以縣界冥水爲名。

translations.literal: *Bi's Collations*: should read Ming'an; *Yuanhe Junxian Records* names the county after Ming River.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan cites hydronym.

translations.literal: Commentary: Bi's argument stands—emend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Editors adopt Ming'an.

translations.literal: Same correction applies below.
translations.idiomatic: Following entries mirror this fix.

sentences.zh: 深泉考異：「淵泉」作「深泉」，避唐諱。

translations.literal: Shenquan textual note: ‘Yuanquan’ became Shenquan under Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Tang editors dodged Li Yuan's name.

sentences.zh: 張駿分武威武興西平張掖酒泉建康西海西郡湟河晉興廣武合十一郡爲涼州 原缺「西海」，「廣武」誤作「須武」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》補改。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun split Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xi, Huanghe, Jinxing, Guangwu into Liangzhou — original omitted ‘Xihai’ and misprinted Guangwu as ‘Xuwu’; now corrected per *Wei Shu · Zhang Jun biography.*
translations.idiomatic: Modern editors therefore plug Xihai back into Zhang Jun's elevenfold Liangzhou list and restore Guangwu where older prints mangled it into Xuwu, following Zhang Jun's biography in Wei Shu.

sentences.zh: 敦煌晉昌高昌西域都護戊己校尉玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州 原缺「高昌」，「戊己」誤作「張茂以」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》增改。

translations.literal: Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, Western Regions protector, Wuji colonel, Yumen grand protector — original omitted ‘Gaochang’ and misread Wuji as ‘Zhang Mao yi’; amended per *Wei Shu · Zhang Jun biography.*
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu restores Gaochang and Wuji titles.

translations.literal: ‘Jin restored Tianshui’ — ‘Jin’ should read ‘Wei.’
translations.idiomatic: Wei, not Jin, revived Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 魏時有天水郡，見三國志姜維傳及注、楊阜傳、曹真傳、張既傳、閻溫傳。

translations.literal: Wei era retained Tianshui Commandery—see Jiang Wei, Yang Fu, Cao Zhen, Zhang Ji, and Yan Wen's biographies in *Records of the Three Kingdoms.*
translations.idiomatic: Three Kingdoms notices prove Wei-period seat.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝初平六年趙一清水經注釋三三：全祖望謂初平只四年，無六年，當作元年。

translations.literal: ‘Emperor Xian Chuping sixth year’ — Zhao Yi *Shui Jing commentary* 33: Quan Zuwang notes Chuping lasted four years, so ‘six’ must be ‘first year.’
translations.idiomatic: Chronology critics fix regnal year.

sentences.zh: 縣四十四各本作「縣三十三」，今從殿本作「縣四十四」，與統計實數合。

translations.literal: ‘Forty-four counties’ — editions read thirty-three; Palace prints forty-four, matching statistical totals.
translations.idiomatic: Palace county tally matches.

sentences.zh: 蜀置 《畢校》：譙周《巴記》，建安六年劉璋分巴郡墊江以上爲巴西郡。

translations.literal: ‘Shu established’ — *Bi's Collations*: Qiao Zhou's *Ba Chronicle* says Liu Zhang split Ba commandery north of Dianjiang into Baxi in Jian'an 6.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou dates Liu Zhang's split.

sentences.zh: 據此，則巴西郡劉璋時分置。

translations.literal: Hence Baxi Commandery dates to Liu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Line clarifies Liu Zhang's foundation.

sentences.zh: 魚復各本作「魚腹」，今從宋本作「魚復」。

translations.literal: Yufu — editions write ‘fish belly’ except Song prints preserving ‘Yufu.’
translations.idiomatic: Song restores Yufu against mistaken ‘fish belly.’

sentences.zh: 漢志上、《續漢志·五》、華陽國志一、後漢書張堪傳、蜀志先主傳並作「魚復」。

translations.literal: Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise V, *Huayang Annals* I, Fan Ye's Zhang Kan biography, and Liu Bei's Founder biography all write ‘Yufu.’
translations.idiomatic: Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise V, Huayang Annals book one, Fan Ye's Zhang Kan biography, and Chen Shou's Shu Founder biography unanimously preserve the Yufu spelling.

sentences.zh: 初平元年劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡考異：劉焉以興平元年卒，子璋始爲益州牧，則初平元年璋尚未牧益州，「初平」當爲「興平」之訛。

translations.literal: ‘Chuping first year Liu Zhang split Ba for Yongning’ — textual note: Liu Yan died Xingping first year; Liu Zhang became shepherd afterward—‘Chuping’ must miswrite ‘Xingping.’
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Yan died in Xingping 1 and only afterward did Liu Zhang inherit Yizhou, the headline era cannot be Chuping 1—scribes must read Xingping.

translations.literal: Zhiyuan originally read ‘Yuanzhi.’
translations.idiomatic: Characters reversed.

sentences.zh: 斠注：兩漢志、華陽國志四並作「談指」。

translations.literal: Jiao commentary: both Han treatises and *Huayang Annals* IV write Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sources agree on order Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 按：漢書昭帝紀、前漢紀十六亦作「談指」。

translations.literal: Commentary: Han Emperor Zhao annals and Qian Han Ji 16 likewise write Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han court histories agree.

translations.literal: Characters transposed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Editors swap order.

translations.literal: Wuxian originally read ‘Wujian.’
translations.idiomatic: Second graph corrupted.

sentences.zh: 斠注：兩漢志、宋志、華陽國志四、水經溫水注皆作「毋歛」。

translations.literal: Jiao commentary: both Han treatises, Song treatise, *Huayang Annals* IV, and Shui Jing Wen River gloss write Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Broad consensus on Wuxian.

translations.literal: Commentary: ‘jian’ is wrong—emend.
translations.idiomatic: Graph correction.

sentences.zh: 毋掇漢志上「掇」作「棳」，師古曰其字從木。

translations.literal: Wuduo — Han Treatise I writes ‘duo’ with wood radical; Yan Shigu says the wood form is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Orthographic note from Hanshu.

translations.literal: Shui Jing Wen River gloss likewise writes ‘Wuduo.’
translations.idiomatic: Hydrology agrees.

translations.literal: Tanfeng — editions write ‘duo’ except Song and phonological glosses reading ‘tan.’
translations.idiomatic: Bronze versus bell phonetics.

sentences.zh: 宋本及音義作「鐔」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Song prints and pronunciation guides read ‘tan’—follow Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song preserves Tan graph.

sentences.zh: 與漢志上、《續漢志·五》、宋志四、華陽國志四、水經溫水注合。

translations.literal: Matches Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise V, Song Treatise IV, *Huayang Annals* IV, and Shui Jing Wen gloss.
translations.idiomatic: Those witnesses march in step with Han Treatise I, Xu Han Treatise V, Song geography book four, Huayang Annals book four, and Li Daoyuan's commentary on the Wen River.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年至夜郎二郡 王遜傳：「元帝加遜安南將軍，刺史如故。

translations.literal: ‘Yongjia second year to Yelang twin commanderies’ — Wang Xun's biography: ‘Emperor Yuan promoted Wang Xun to south-pacifying general while keeping him inspector.’
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun biography excerpt begins.

sentences.zh: 遜表請改分牂牁爲平夷郡，分建寧爲夜郎郡，改益州爲晉寧郡，事皆施行。

translations.literal: ‘Xun memorialized to carve Zangke into Pingyi Commandery, split Jianning into Yelang Commandery, and rename Yizhou Commandery Jinning—all approved.’
translations.idiomatic: Memorial describes adjustments.

translations.literal: "」This diverges from this treatise's wording."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun's account clashes with the geography chapter.
